profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public technology company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. With last reported annual revenue of $215.938 billion as of January 25, 2026, the company describes itself as building agentic AI with multimodal foundation models. The company's website presents NVIDIA Nemotron as a family of highly efficient, multimodal, open AI models designed for long-running, self-evolving agents that deliver reasoning capabilities for graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding.

NVIDIA tracks two AI products: NVIDIA Nemotron, an enterprise large language model family with synthetic data generation and GPU-optimized, self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options. According to its site, Nemotron models are built for fast task completion with high reasoning throughput and leading accuracy for complex agent workflows. The models excel in reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech, and safety tasks. Nemotron Speech models provide automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation for agentic AI. The company publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license allowing commercial deployment without requiring attribution.

NVIDIA operates as a for-profit public company with stock ticker NVDA and CIK 0001045810. The company faces significant legal exposure in California with 220 tracked cases. The company does not maintain an MCP server registry presence and has no tracked SEC filings or patent facts in the held data.
